why: The strict provenance gate (scripts/validate_provenance.py --require-approved) fails at every head to date. It was wired into no CI job, so it read as a passing gate to anyone who saw it in the tree. This ledger records the exact failure set so CI can enforce it: the gate now runs on every push, and the build fails if the failure set grows, shrinks, or changes shape. It cannot pass until a maintainer records the decisions listed in `blocked_on`.
how_this_is_enforced: scripts/check_provenance_ratchet.py runs the strict gate, compares its error set to `errors` below, and fails on any difference in either direction. A growing list is new unrecorded provenance debt; a shrinking list means someone made a real decision and this ledger must be updated in the same change.
not_a_waiver: Recording a blocker here does not assert its claim is true. Most entries are unapproved status transitions; the SBML Test Suite entry is an observed corpus pin whose role and acceptance still require a maintainer decision. The repository is honest about being unapproved; this ledger makes that state machine-checked instead of invisible.
invariants_that_must_hold: The set below is the COMPLETE strict error set, not a subset. A new source, oracle, or dependency added to upstreams.lock.yml while unapproved MUST appear here or CI fails.
No entry may be deleted to make the gate green. Each requires a recorded human decision (see blocked_on), which is a provenance change to upstreams.lock.yml, not an edit to this file.
